steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add onion and bell pepper; cook until onion is tender and golden and bell pepper is slightly soft, about 10 minutes. Stir in balsamic vinegar; season with salt and black pepper.
Rub tilapia fillets with 2 teaspoons olive oil; season with salt and black pepper. Place fillets in a small baking dish; top with balsamic-onion mixture. Sprinkle with blue cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until tilapia flakes easily with a fork; serve on salad greens.

raw_recipe.headline: Balsamic Baked Tilapia
raw_recipe.description: In this balsamic baked tilapia recipe, balsamic vinegar add sweetness to the onions and peppers that top the fillets along with crumbled blue cheese.
raw_recipe.name: Balsamic Baked Tilapia

review.reviewBody: This was delicious. I added some zuchinni to the onion and red pepper. I also used good cheddar instead of blue cheese. Will serve this again.

We tried this tonight using tangerine Balsamic vinegar, served it over brown rice with sauteed asparagus, and found it delicious. I will make this again, but will increase the Balsamic to three tablespoons and will add some minced garlic.

Wow! Great tasting recipe that I had some initial doubts about. Blue cheese and fish??? Yes, it works especially as a foil to the sweet peppers and the onion, not to mention the pairing with the balsamic vinegar. One addition I made was to sautee some sliced mushrooms after the onions and peppers cooked down a bit. I did not add a full cup of blue cheese as I thought it would be too much. Instead, I added about a scant quarter cup. I served it over buttered orzo with pecorino romano, salt and pepper. Husband thought it was company-worthy and a great dish that he raved about four separate times! Can't wait to make again over the mixed greens.

Very good! I used a lite balsamic vinegar dressing drizzled over fillets arranged in baking dish. I didn't measure, approximately 1/4 c. Then I cut my fresh vegetables, yellow and zucchini squash, orange and yellow sweet peppers; Sautéd in olive oil and arranged on top of fish, then sprinkled with fresh chopped green onions and sparsely drizzled with blue cheese dressing; all because that's what I had on hand. I served this with buttered egg noodles, although I wanted to prepare rice but didn't have enough. Will definitely make it again but will use more balsamic dressing so we have more sauce to drizzle over noodles which turned out to be a good compliment.

very tasty and a touch gourmet! like most people on here, i didnt have any blue cheese so i substituted it with Feta cheese. i also added blackening seasoning to the tilapia for a little extra flavor. the directions dont mention the amount of time to bake the Tilapia so i just put it in for 20min at 350 degrees and it was perfect. i plated the fish on top of green beans tossed with basil garlic butter sauce. (instead of basil i would have rather used fresh chopped cilantro but didnt have any) The two dishes married together very well and was all around delicious and healthy!

This was delicious, will definitely make again. Before baking, I sprinkled the fish with Sazon Tropical, and added a little balsamic salad dressing in the bottom of the pan. I used two shallots in place of the onion, and added a little chopped jalapeno. I added red pepper flakes to the oil. I omitted the cheese (as my daughter doesn't eat cheese), and baked for 18 minutes at 375. The fish was flavorful and not dry. Served over yellow rice - thanks for sharing!
041923- Riley only likes salmon. Need to work on it a little more. Good for everyone else. Served with Rice and green beans with mushrooms. Used Feta instead of Bleu Cheese. 021522 5 stars.

Good way to jazz up a normally pretty bland fish. I added some cherry tomatoes to the onion and bell pepper. Was a little generous with the balsamic. Added feta after it came out of oven. Nice change of pace . . .
Great recipe! Not a blue cheese fan so left it out completely, used melted butter with sautéed garlic over the fish instead of oil and I added thin carrots as well. We really enjoyed this.

This recipe was delicous and is definitely a keeper. Don't be afraid of the cheese!! I cooked at 375 for about 15 min, also added zuchinni to the veggies. I would guess whatever fresh veggies you have to saute would work equally as well... (asparagus, julienned carrots, etc.). I served over greens as recipe suggests; however I bet rice would be great too as others have mentioned. Will definitely make again! Served with a grilled peach with balsamic glaze - what a yummy end to this dish!

Made this for dinner on Sunday for a big group. I know it was a hit because my brother, who is a gourmet cook even asked for the recipe. I did as a few others suggested and swapped feta for the blue cheese. Instead of just salt & pepper, I sprinkled lightly with Old Bay seafood seasoning but want to try a blackened or creole spice next. I also did a balsamic reduction with about 1/2 c. vinegar. When the fish is finished from the oven and plated atop the greens - drizzle the thickened vinegar lightly over the top of fish and pepper/onion mixture. Looks and tastes wonderful!
One of my all time favorite recipes 😋
Wow. So easy and delicious and impressive. My friend took a picture of it!
Made it as written. Only fair as the good quality blue cheese overpowered the fish. Might be a 4* if less blue cheese used.
Did feta instead and everyone loved it. Did anyone try it with chicken? My brother and wife are allergic to fish

This was a great recipe for tilapia added a lot of flavor. I only gave it 4 stars because it has no instructions in the recipe for how long to cook it! I ended up having to check it every 10 minutes or so and finally took it out after about 20-25 minutes. Followed the recipe as written except: used Parmesan cheese (don’t care for either blue or feta cheese) - and next time I will use mozzarella - and added some halved cherry tomatoes to the top. I did serve it on some salad greens per the recipe and that was a very nice touch - especially with the tomatoes!
My husband usually says that tilapia is so bland, but not with this recipe! We both absolutely loved it, and I will make it again.

Like others, I used feta instead of blue cheese because that was what I had, but I will try it again with blue cheese, which sounds amazing. My husband and I really liked the color and flavor of this dish, which improved an otherwise rather bland fish, and it's light and healthy too!
Great recipe. Made this with sun dried tomatoes in place of peppers. And Romano in place of blue cheese.
